summary: Bursting short-lived inference streams causing slot serialization and p99 throughput drift in Dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: SecuraHealth reports sudden P99 throughput degradation on their dedicated pool that correlates with a spike in short-duration inference streams (avg 50-200ms). Impact: customer-facing endpoints see p99 latency increase and effective throughput drop of ~18% for batched routes. Environment: Dedicated pool (prod-us-west), pinned to redwood-7b-v2, default batching profile, autoscaler configured with min=2 max=12. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run a mix of long streams (multi-second requests) and high-frequency short streams (50-200ms). 2) Observe batch slots and kernel queues via /internal/metrics for the pool. 3) Notice accumulation at kernel queue tail and serialized batch execution. Observed behavior: short-lived requests create many tiny batches that serialize on slots leading to kernel queue tail latency; this prevents larger multi-token requests from filling batches efficiently, causing throughput collapse at P99. Expected behavior: small short-lived requests should be buffered into micro-batches without starving larger batched workloads; autoscaler should smooth minor spikes without slot serialization. Workaround in place: customer temporarily routed short-lived endpoints to a separate dedicated route with lower batching (reduced concurrency) to isolate impact.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy small scale reproduction using redwood-7b-v2 in a dedicated pool with min=2, max=12 GPUs
Generate a steady stream of long requests (1-2s) at 10 qps and concurrent bursty short requests (50-200ms) at 40 qps for 10 minutes
Collect metrics: serving.kernel_queue_length, serving.slot_utilization, batching.latency_per_batch, scheduler.enqueue_time
Observe batch sizes and kernel queue tail latency during bursts
investigation_notes: Initial triage: pattern matches slot serialization rather than GPU exhaustion — GPU util steady at 64-72% while p99 increases
Hypothesis 1: micro-bursts create many single-request batches which tie up slot locks (KV cache and kernel mutex) leading to head-of-line blocking for larger batches

Hypothesis 2: scheduler backpressure thresholding currently prioritizes fairness evenly but doesn't account for high variance short-tail workloads — causing frequent context switches and kernel rebind penalties
Metric evidence: batch_size distribution shifted from median=16 to median=3 during incident window; kernel_rebinds metric increased by 4x
Related signals: increased PCIe peer-to-peer stall traces in trace logs when tiny batches executed in rapid succession
Reference runbook: linked Confluence page on Dedicated pool slot modeling for mitigation steps

mitigation_attempts: Route isolation: moved short-lived endpoints to a separate dedicated route — immediate reduction in P99 for main route (restored by ~15%)
Batching tweaks: increased micro-batching window from 6ms to 12ms reduced single-batch counts by ~35% but added 5-8ms median latency
Autoscaler tuning: increased min_reachable_slots to reduce slot churn; prevented immediate oscillation but did not remove serialization entirely
root_cause: High-frequency short-lived inference streams produce many single-request micro-batches that hold slot/kernel resources briefly but frequently, causing kernel queue tail latency and head-of-line blocking for larger batches. Scheduler fairness policy and micro-batching window were not adaptive to high variance request duration, enabling noisy short streams to serialize slot use.
resolution_plan: Short term (next 72 hours): recommend customers isolate high-variance short endpoints into separate routes and apply temporary micro-batching window increase (12ms) — update runbook and notify SecuraHealth

Medium term (2-3 weeks): implement adaptive micro-batching window that expands under detected high-variance tails and a lightweight per-route backpressure token so short streams cannot immediately occupy slot mutexes

Long term (1-2 months): scheduler change to prefer batch assembly prioritization for multi-token requests when queued alongside short single-token requests, and add kernel rebind suppression when consecutive tiny batches detected
